extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of CCR units, regulated electric utilities, State regulators, and environmental/stakeholder commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule preamble describing statutory authority, scope, and substantive regulatory requirements that make legacy CCR surface impoundments and certain CCR management units (CCRMU) subject to 40 CFR part 257, subpart D, and listing specific compliance obligations, deadlines, and technical corrections. Also summarizes risk assessment and economic analysis supporting the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of rule provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA intends the provisions of the rule to be severable. In the event that any individual provision or part of the rule is invalidated, EPA intends that this would not render the entire rule invalid, and that any individual provisions that can continue to operate will be left in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA gives example that provisions governing each class of facilities (legacy CCR inactive surface impoundments, CCR management units, other active facility units, and regulated CCR landfills containing waste in contact with groundwater) are independently severable; within sets of provisions, substantive requirements (e.g., closure requirements vs groundwater monitoring/corrective action) are intended to be severable so that remaining requirements can continue to operate if another is set aside.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for action (RCRA sections cited)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is publishing this notice under the authority of sections 1008(a), 2002(a), 3007, 4004, and 4005(a) and (d) of the Solid Waste Disposal Act (RCRA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory provisions form the legal basis for promulgating minimum criteria, distinguishing sanitary landfills from open dumps, requiring closing/upgrading open dumps, and for the special CCR provisions allowing State permit programs or EPA permits to operate in lieu of Federal regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCRA section 1008(a)(3) enforceable guideline scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to section 1008(a)(3), the guidelines are to include the minimum criteria to be used by the States to define the solid waste management practices that constitute the open dumping of solid waste or hazardous waste and are prohibited as 'open dumping' under section 4005.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only those requirements promulgated under the authority of section 1008(a)(3) are enforceable under section 7002 of RCRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCRA section 4004(a) sanitary landfill standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4004(a) generally requires EPA to promulgate regulations containing criteria distinguishing 'sanitary landfills,' which may continue to operate, from 'open dumps,' which are prohibited. At a minimum, the criteria are to ensure that units are classified as sanitary landfills only if there is no reasonable probability of adverse effects on health or the environment from disposal of solid wastes at such facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA interprets this standard to apply equally to criteria issued under sections 1008(a)(3) and 4004(a), and to authorize establishment of criteria that define how facilities upgrade or close to ensure no reasonable probability of adverse effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCRA section 4005(a) prohibition and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: RCRA section 4005(a) prohibits any solid waste management practices or disposal of solid waste that does not comply with EPA regulations issued under RCRA section 1008(a) and 4004(a). This prohibition takes effect 'upon promulgation'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition is enforceable either through a citizen suit brought pursuant to section 7002, or through an EPA enforcement action brought pursuant to section 4005(d)(4)(A). Section 4005(a) also directs that open dumps must be closed or upgraded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of 40 CFR part 257, subpart D to CCR units (RCRA 4005(d)(3)/(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: RCRA section 4005(d)(3) specifies that the regulations in 40 CFR part 257, subpart D 'shall apply to each CCR unit' unless a permit issued by an approved State or by EPA is in effect. Section 4005(d)(6) provides that a CCR unit shall be considered to be a sanitary landfill only if the unit is operating in accordance with a permit or the applicable criteria under part 257.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes a statutory mechanism where either Federal criteria or an approved State/EPA permit determine whether a CCR unit qualifies as a sanitary landfill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal standards are self-implementing; facility responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal role is to establish minimum nationwide standards that will protect human health and the environment; Federal standards apply directly to the facility (are self-implementing) and facilities are directly responsible for ensuring that their operations comply with these requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may adopt these requirements into their programs but are not required to; until an approved State permit is in effect, facilities must comply with the Federal regulations directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA promulgates requirements without considering cost (statutory constraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under RCRA, EPA sets these requirements without taking cost into account as a factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA notes this in the context of the USWAG decision and frames the economic analysis (RIA) separately, but statutory standard-setting is irrespective of cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA authority to regulate closed/legacy units that continue to pose risks
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA interprets the RCRA provisions to authorize regulation of closed units that continue to pose risks to health or the environment, e.g., by requiring owners or operators to remediate contamination or take action to prevent contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA cites court precedent and statutory definitions (disposal as continuing presence of waste) to support regulating inactive or closed units where risk remains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy CCR surface impoundments made subject to 40 CFR part 257, subpart D
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing a provision at §257.50(e), specifying that legacy CCR surface impoundments are subject to 40 CFR part 257, subpart D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change brings formerly exempt legacy impoundments within the scope of the CCR regulatory framework and triggers associated compliance obligations for owners/operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation of a permanent marker
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments must comply with the existing requirement for installation of a permanent marker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the existing requirements now applicable to legacy impoundments (part of the set that also includes history of construction, hazard classification, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain history of construction documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must comply with existing requirements to maintain a history of construction for the unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the required documentation and recordkeeping applicable to legacy impoundments under 40 CFR part 257, subpart D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazard potential classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must perform and comply with hazard potential classification requirements for legacy CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hazard potential classification informs subsequent requirements such as structural assessments and emergency planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural stability and factors of safety assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must comply with requirements for structural stability and factors of safety assessments for legacy CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These assessments evaluate dam/impoundment safety and are part of the suite of requirements to address catastrophic failure risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency Action Plan (EAP) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must prepare and maintain an Emergency Action Plan (EAP) for legacy CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EAPs are required to mitigate consequences of structural failure or other emergencies and are included among existing CCR requirements applied to legacy units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air criteria applicable to legacy units
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must comply with applicable air criteria under part 257 now made applicable to legacy CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Air criteria were listed among the existing regulatory requirements to be applied to legacy impoundments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspections requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must comply with inspection requirements for legacy CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular structural and operational inspections are required under the CCR regulatory framework and now apply to legacy impoundments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater monitoring and corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must implement groundwater monitoring and corrective action requirements for legacy CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groundwater monitoring scope and corrective action are key components to detect and remediate contamination; EPA indicates corrections to groundwater monitoring scope references in the rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure and post-closure care requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must comply with closure and post-closure care requirements applicable to legacy CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA is also finalizing alternative closure provisions to allow two-stage closure by removal and separate post-closure groundwater remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must comply with recordkeeping requirements applicable to legacy CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA also finalizes an extension of the period for document retention and posting; recordkeeping supports public transparency and regulatory oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and CCR website requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must comply with notification and CCR website posting requirements for legacy CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA is standardizing references to CCR websites throughout the regulations and is extending document posting/retention periods as a technical correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of new compliance deadlines for newly-applicable requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is establishing new compliance deadlines for the newly applicable regulatory requirements to provide owners/operators time to come into compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines are intended to phase in applicability of requirements to legacy units; specific deadlines are set elsewhere in the final rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extending a subset of part 257 requirements to CCR Management Units (CCRMU)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is extending a subset of the existing requirements in 40 CFR part 257, subpart D to CCRMU, which EPA proposed to include CCR surface impoundments and landfills that closed prior to the effective date of the 2015 CCR Rule, inactive CCR landfills, and other areas where CCR is managed directly on the land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These additional requirements apply to all active CCR facilities, all inactive facilities with legacy CCR surface impoundments subject to this final rule, and active facilities that ceased placing CCR in onsite units prior to Oct 19, 2015. The rule indicates EPA will specify which subset of requirements applies to CCRMU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative two-stage closure by removal
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing alternative closure provisions to allow a facility to complete the closure by removal in two stages: first, by completing all removal and decontamination procedures; and second, by completing all groundwater remediation in a separate post closure care period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows sequencing of physical removal and later groundwater remediation while maintaining regulatory oversight during the post-closure care period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical corrections to CFR references and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing technical corrections including clarifying the definitions of 'feasible' and 'technically feasible'; correcting the CFR reference in the definition of wetlands at §257.61(a); correcting a reference in the groundwater monitoring scope section; and standardizing references to CCR websites throughout the CCR regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are textual/clarifying amendments intended to harmonize and correct cross-references and definitions to reduce ambiguity in compliance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of document retention and posting period
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing an extension of the period for document retention and posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technical correction increases how long owners/operators must retain and post CCR-related documents on CCR websites as required by the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory economic analysis (RIA) cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The RIA estimates annualized monetized costs of this action will be approximately $214-$240 million per year when discounting at 2%. Breakdown: $123-$135M for legacy CCR surface impoundments, $79-$92M for CCRMU, $8-$9M for CCRMU at Other Active Facilities (OAFUs), and $4M for landfills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIA includes costs for unit closure, corrective action, fugitive dust controls, structural integrity inspections, and recordkeeping/reporting. EPA notes it establishes requirements under RCRA without regard to cost, but provides the RIA for transparency and to comply with OMB/E.O. guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory economic analysis (RIA) benefits and non-monetized benefit categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The RIA estimates annualized monetized benefits of approximately $53-$80M per year (2% discount). It also describes ten categories of non-monetized benefits including human health effects from lead exposure (e.g., ADHD, cardiovascular mortality, increased cancer risk), ecosystem benefits from avoided heavy metal exposure, property-related benefits including increased property values and option values for remediated land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA uses these monetized and non-monetized benefit descriptions to contextualize the rule's expected public health, ecological, and property-related outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk factors and evidence supporting regulation of legacy units
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA relied on the 2014 Risk Assessment and additional information to find that legacy CCR surface impoundments and CCRMU may pose risks equal to or greater than previously regulated units due to factors such as greater prevalence of unlined units; greater likelihood of co-management with coal refuse and other wastes (making waste pH more acidic); units present onsite longer and thus having more time to leak; and potential construction below the water table or post-construction inundation with groundwater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA estimated potential lifetime cancer risks and noncancer hazard quotients for various constituents under these management practices and used this evidence to justify applying subpart D requirements to legacy impoundments and CCRMU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior and supplemental risk assessments and solicitation of data (NODA/ANPRM inputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA relied on the 2014 Risk Assessment and a 2023 Draft Risk Assessment and published a Notice of Data Availability (NODA) soliciting additional information to inform the final rule and supplemental risk assessment (2024 Risk Assessment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA requested data on locations, unit status (capped/dry/closed/still holding water), names/locations/closure dates of former power plants, presence of water, distance to surface water bodies, proximity to floodplains, unit size, CCR volume, depth to groundwater, date of CCR placement, closure status, corrective actions, and groundwater monitoring data. EPA used comments and submitted data to update risk analyses and support the final rule.
